newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals-Dull demand haunts industry, trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals-Dull demand haunts industry, trade.

text.p: India's state-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd (HCL) reduced copper wire bar and rod prices by 6,000 rupees per tonne on Wednesday but traders said the move might not spur demand.
"I doubt if the market will revive because of this reduction in HCL prices. Where is the demand for copper?" asked Bombay Metal Exchange president Sharad Parikh.
He said a demand slump in certain key sectors of the economy that consumed non-ferrous metals had affected both industry and trade in the last one year.
Indian non-ferrous metal prices generally reflect LME trends as India imports most metals except aluminium.
But Parikh said he did not see any link between the cut in HCL prices and a subdued trend in copper prices on the London Metal Exchange in the last few days.
Parikh said HCL cut its prices to 13,500 rupees per quintal (100 kg) compared to 14,500 rupees for imported copper wire bar. It traded around 13,650 rupees in the market.
"Traders will have to sell their stocks at or below HCL prices. They will suffer losses. It's not good for trade," Parikh said.

The state-run Hindustan Zinc Ltd raised prices by 3,000 rupees per tonne as demand for zinc picked up because of a shortage of stocks, traders said. They said a ban on imports of zinc ash and dross that went into manufacture of ingots had affected supplies of the metal in the last one year.
Nickel and zinc were subdued in the domestic market on lack demand and lower LME prices.
In the week to Wednesday, copper fell 50 rupees to 13,650 rupees per quintal. Aluminium was steady at 7,700 rupees per quintal. Zinc gained 50 rupees to 8,150.
Tin and nickel lost 200 rupees and 300 rupees per quintal to 29,000 and 33,800 rupees per quintal respectively. This week's and last week's prices were as follows, in rupees per quintal
